claim: Open Loyalty is an API-first, headless 'gamified loyalty engine' (points, multi-wallets, tiers, rewards/coupons, challenges, referrals, games incl. Spin the Wheel / Scratch & Win / lotteries, badges, leaderboards) positioned as 'the Gamified Loyalty Engine behind 100+ enterprise brands' with named clients Aldo, Heineken, Intersport, BAT, limango, Club Brugge.
notes: Homepage also claims $4B+ revenue generated, 400+ programs, 19,700 campaigns, 30 countries, 1B loyalty events/month.

claim: Marketing claims: '120 ms avg API response time', '99.99% guaranteed uptime', '1B loyalty events/month', '75M transactions/year'; business logic 'lives in the engine and is controlled entirely via REST API'.
notes: Marketing numbers; 120ms is API response latency for CRUD/event ingestion, not a synchronous decision latency. Docs SLA states 99.9% (see -003).

claim: Two environments offered: Production (99.9% uptime SLA, zero-downtime upgrades, soft limit 1,200 concurrent req/s, login endpoints 20 RPM) in AWS regions Dublin eu-west-1, Frankfurt eu-central-1, Ohio us-east-2, Singapore ap-southeast-1, Sydney ap-southeast-2; Staging (PoC/functional testing, no SLA, 50 req/s, 'PII is not recommended') in Dublin, Ohio, Sydney.
page_title: Environments & Capabilities | Open Loyalty Technical Guide
notes: Docs say 99.9% uptime while pricing/marketing pages say 99.99% - discrepancy recorded.

claim: Campaigns are triggered by six event types: Purchase Transaction, Return Transaction, Internal Event (e.g. tier updated, member registered/activated), Custom Event ('events sourced from an external system or application'), Achievement completed, Redemption Code.
notes: Internal events documented: Achievement Progressed, Member Address/Company/Profile Details Updated, Member Tier Updated, Member Was Activated.

claim: Campaign rule model: max 6 rules per campaign and 30 conditions total; conditions evaluate tier, purchase history, custom attributes; effects are Add/Deduct Units (formula-based), Give Reward, Set/Remove Member Custom Attribute, Grant Badge, Assign Tier; visibility (who sees) is separated from conditions (who earns). No draft state, versioning, or priority ordering documented.
notes: Output model is reward effects, not allow/deny/review decisions.

claim: Campaign limitations: per-member completion limits (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly/total), global unit budget for the whole campaign, per-member unit budget; limits enforced on the business date of the event; 'If a unit transfer issued by the campaign is canceled, those units are automatically returned to the available pool.'
notes: Static caps for abuse/budget control; no fraud scoring.

claim: Custom conditions and custom effects can be written in an expression meta-language 'based on the expression syntax of Symfony Expression' (strings, numbers, arrays, hashes, booleans, null, scientific notation); expressions limited to 500 characters.
notes: Sample use cases include if/else complex effects, excluding members, tier upgrade/downgrade differentiation.

claim: Expressions can access rich stateful context: customer.* (profile, address incl. country/province/postal, consents legalConsent/marketingConsent/dataProcessingConsent, tier, registeredDate, transaction stats, per-wallet activeUnits/spentUnits/earnedUnits/lockedUnits/blockedUnits/expiredUnits), transaction.* (items by SKU/category/brand, labels, grossValue, channelId), event.body.* for custom events, and executionContext.processedAt.
notes: Geographic attributes (country/province/postal) are declared member data, not verified geolocation.

claim: Campaign simulation (UI + API endpoint 'simulate campaigns result') lets admins test which campaigns would fire and what rewards would be granted for a given trigger, member and transaction/event input before go-live; providing a Member ID auto-imports stored member details into the simulator.
notes: Single-scenario dry-run; no population-level impact analysis; always evaluates current configuration (no historical replay).

claim: Conflict/order handling is limited: 'When several campaigns are activated by the same trigger, they are executed in order of their Campaign Start Date, with the earliest one being executed first.' No priority field or conflict-resolution model documented.

Campaign effects are applied asynchronously after event ingestion: adding a transaction via POST /api/{storeCode}/transaction 'should trigger CampaignEffectWasApplied webhook' - i.e., the API response confirms ingestion and effects are delivered via webhooks/state changes, not returned synchronously as a decision.
page_title: Add Transaction | Open Loyalty Technical Guide
notes: Key architectural distinction vs synchronous decision engines (e.g., Talon.One); no allow/deny gate in the request path.

claim: Webhook event catalog includes TransactionRegistered, AvailablePointsAmountChanged, TransactionAssignedToCustomer, CampaignEffectWasApplied, PointsWillExpire, WalletBalanceUpdated, RewardRedemptionStatusChanged, CustomerBoughtReward, CouponWillExpire, CustomerRegistered, CustomerUpdated, CustomerLevelChanged, LevelWillExpire, CustomerDeactivated and more.
page_title: What Triggers a Webhook | Open Loyalty
notes: Docs point to API reference as source of truth for full list and payload schemas.

claim: Webhooks support HMAC-SHA256 signatures ('attaches a cryptographic signature to every webhook request'), one-time-display secret keys, and a rotate-HMAC-secret-key API endpoint; webhook subscriptions are manageable via API and admin UI.
notes: Retry policy/delivery guarantees not documented on this page; webhook delivery to AWS SQS documented separately.

claim: Audit API: GET /api/audit/log returns entries with auditLogId, store (nested tenant object), eventType, entityType, entityId, username, userId, userType, ip, createdAt; filterable by eventType, entityId, entityType, username, IP, userType, store, createdAt; additional endpoints create/export/download system-log archives and exports.
page_title: Get All System Logs | Open Loyalty API Reference
notes: Retention policy and tamper-evidence/immutability are not documented.

claim: The system log (Admin Cockpit, admin-only) records member-data events (registration, updates, viewing, activation, deactivation, anonymization, deletion), authentication events (login success/failure, session expiry, token refresh), ACL role create/modify/delete, admin account create/edit, audit-log viewing/exporting, and transaction viewing; each record has date/time, type, unique change ID, and user name; CSV export with time-range selection.
notes: Human ACTION history, not approval history - no approval workflow exists to record.

claim: Campaign Execution export records one row per campaign execution with campaignExecutionId, tenantId, campaignId, customerId, transactionId, contextData ('Context data that triggered the campaign (e.g. member's data, transaction data)'), executionStatus (success/skipped/failed), executedAt, createdAt/updatedAt, message and warningMessage for failures.
page_title: Campaign Execution | Open Loyalty Data Exports
notes: Input facts captured per execution; does not record per-condition evaluation results, and campaignId is not linked to a campaign VERSION.

claim: Campaign Calculated Effect Results export records per-effect outcomes: calculatedEffectResultId, tenantId, campaignExecutionId (links to parent execution), status (success/skipped/failed), targetId (member), type (e.g. give_points, give_reward), points, couponValue, rewardId, walletCode, error.
page_title: Campaign Calculated Effect Results | Open Loyalty Data Exports
notes: Establishes provenance chain: campaign execution -> effect -> units/reward in wallet.

claim: Daily automated data exports: 'Every day (after midnight), Open Loyalty generates CSV files containing the data changes (deltas) from the previous day' delivered to customer AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage; positioned for financial liability tracking, campaign analysis, and data warehousing/BI.
page_title: Data Exports Overview | Open Loyalty Technical Guide
notes: Batch (daily) evidence export, not an on-demand regulator package.

claim: Tenants (previously 'Stores') allow 'many tenants with different currencies, codes, and names' in one installation; per-tenant members, transactions, campaigns, rewards, custom events, translations; global (cross-tenant) areas are Configuration, Administrators, Roles, Tenants management; tenants have a timezone strategy (Default or Local time) and auto-deactivate-campaigns setting.
notes: Multi-tenant is how multi-country programs (e.g., JTI 18 countries) are structured; pricing page: 'separate tenants per country/project'.

claim: Timezone semantics are tenant-based: 'Campaign rules and achievement triggers are based on the tenant's configured timezone'; event timestamps with other offsets are converted and stored in the tenant timezone; the same UTC event can fall inside a campaign window in one tenant and outside it in another.
notes: Temporal rule evaluation is deterministic per tenant timezone.

claim: RBAC/ACL: custom roles grant View (read-only) or Modify (create/edit/delete/run) per resource across Tenants, Settings (ACL, Admins, Audit log, Channels, Languages), Members, Segments, Transactions, Analytics, Global management, Rewards, Imports/Exports, Wallets, Webhooks, Collections, Tiers, Campaigns; roles manageable via ACL API endpoints.
notes: Only View/Modify levels exist - no approve/review permission level and no maker-checker workflow.

claim: SSO via OpenID Connect (OIDC) is supported for administrator authentication with step-by-step guides for Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.
page_title: Enabling SSO Login | Open Loyalty Technical Guide
notes: OIDC only; SAML not documented. Scope is admin panel, not loyalty members.

claim: Backward-compatibility policy: 'We guarantee that our updates will not break backward compatibility'; new capabilities ship as 'versioned endpoints'; when migration is needed 'You will have three months to migrate or adjust your systems accordingly'; changes roll out to staging then production with 'no downtime during updates'.

Documented API limits: auth endpoints 20 RPM per client (rising to 40 RPM effective 2026-09-15), 30-second API timeout, max _page=500 on list endpoints (currently 50, enforced 2026-09-15), 5 concurrent import/export files, 100MB max import file, 255-char strings, 500-char expressions; loyalty card numbers unique per tenant.
notes: 429 responses documented in best practices; 1,200 req/s production soft limit in environments doc.

claim: Multiple configurable wallet types per program with custom unit names; five expiration methods (never, after X days, end of month, end of X-th year, annual date); pending periods ('Pending units stay locked until the waiting period ends'); optional negative balances ('spend units even without enough available balance'); global and per-member automatic-transfer caps.
page_title: Wallet Types and Configuration | Open Loyalty
notes: Member expression context exposes per-wallet active/spent/earned/locked/blocked/expired unit counters.

claim: Unit transfers form the wallet ledger covering 'Manual changes created by admins, Spending events from reward redemption, System events such as peer-to-peer transfers, Expired or blocked units'; API endpoints add/spend/block/cancel/expire/activate unit transfers and update transfer labels; transfers importable/exportable.
notes: Endpoint list corroborated by API reference sitemap (points/* endpoints).

claim: Open Loyalty holds ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certifications, first achieved November 2022, renewed annually (most recently September 2025), certified by DEKRA; 2024 transition to ISO 27001:2022 revision; platform 'periodically tested against OWASP top 10 and CWE/SANS top 25'.
page_title: Open Loyalty achieves ISO 9001 and ISO 27001
notes: No SOC 2 attestation mentioned anywhere on site or docs.

claim: Pricing is usage-based and sales-led: Platform Fee + Allowance Fee driven by monthly Active Members ('a Registered Member who performs at least one Loyalty Event per calendar month'); includes full API access, no feature limits, 24/7 monitoring, P1 response <30 minutes and resolution <2 hours, '99.99%' guaranteed uptime; SaaS cloud with data storage options in Europe, APAC, North America; encryption at rest/in transit; separate Kubernetes namespaces per customer; GDPR/CCPA compliance claimed.
notes: No dollar figures published. Official page, but SLA numbers differ from technical docs (99.9%).

claim: Case-study roster spans regulated and multi-country enterprises: JTI 'Builds a D2C Loyalty Program Across 18 Countries', British American Tobacco 'B2B Loyalty Programs Across Europe and America', ALDO 'Implements a global loyalty program in 3 months', U.S. Soccer, Heineken Vietnam, Circles.Life (telecom), Drop Tank (US fuel), banks (Asia Commercial Bank, Warba Bank, Yoyo), insurers (Prudential Vietnam PRUrewards, EFU Life), Intersport Denmark, Club Brugge, MSI, Zambrero, Borrowell, SeQura.
page_title: Our Clients and Loyalty Case Studies - Open Loyalty
notes: Presence in tobacco, alcohol, banking, insurance, fuel = customers operating in regulated categories, though Open Loyalty provides no regulatory features.

claim: Open Loyalty was created inside Polish eCommerce company Divante (Wroclaw, Poland), building loyalty technology since ~2018, and secured EUR 2.3M R&D investment (EUR 1.3M from Poland's National Center for Research and Development, remainder from Divante).
page_title: Headless loyalty platform Open Loyalty secured 2.3M euro to expand its fintech technology
notes: From parent-company news page via search snippets; small-company scale relative to enterprise loyalty suites.

claim: The historical open-source edition (PHP/Symfony with Broadway CQRS/event sourcing) is no longer hosted in the official GitHub org - the org now contains only dormant Hyperledger Fabric 'loyalty-blockchain' side projects (last updated 2023, Apache-2.0), api-docs, and utilities; third-party fork READMEs state the open-source edition was 'limited for projects with up to 200 members... recommended for testing purposes only'.
notes: Inference: current product is closed-source SaaS; legacy docs at docs.openloyalty.io describe the old architecture (Symfony, Doctrine, Broadway event sourcing).

claim: Official MCP server (@open-loyalty/mcp-server) exposes 'the Open Loyalty API as a set of MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools' - 145 tools across 22 domains (members, points/wallets, tiers, rewards, campaigns and simulation, segments, achievements, transactions, analytics, audit, webhooks, imports/exports, custom events) - for AI agents like Claude Desktop/Code and Cursor; auth via OPENLOYALTY_API_URL/API_TOKEN env vars.
page_title: MCP Server | Open Loyalty Technical Guide
notes: Docs advise treating write actions as proposals with human oversight.

claim: Segments support 27 condition types including demographics (age range, gender, country, city, province, postal code), purchase behavior (spend/transaction counts by period and channel), product/brand/SKU purchases, member tier, custom attributes, admin-curated member lists, achievement completion/progression, and custom events in last X days.
notes: Recalculation cadence (real-time vs scheduled) not documented.

claim: Automation Campaigns run on schedules without external triggers: Daily/Weekly/Monthly at 00:00 tenant time, Birthday, and Anniversary triggers; rule conditions filter by segment, tier, custom attributes; audience capped at 200,000 members (birthday/anniversary exempt); maximum 4 automation campaigns per program.

Fortune Wheels implement instant-win-style mechanics: independent per-spin probability ('The drawing system has no memory'), with a Business Logic Layer that overrides probability - 'Even if the wheel lands on a win, the system checks your configuration before awarding the prize' - blocking wins when reward inventory is depleted, campaign budget/spin limits are reached, or member daily/total win limits are exceeded.
page_title: How Probability Works | Open Loyalty Fortune Wheels
notes: No certified-drawing, odds-disclosure, or sweepstakes-law features; homepage also lists Scratch & Win and lotteries as game types.

claim: GDPR support: 'you have the option to either anonymize member data or remove members entirely'; member profiles carry legalConsent, marketingConsent, dataProcessingConsent booleans; anonymize-members-data and delete-member API endpoints exist.
notes: Consent flags are data fields; no consent-lifecycle or legal-basis management tooling documented.

claim: Configuration portability: Config Duplication copies wallets, custom event schemas, rewards, segments, achievements, campaigns, referral campaigns, and automations between tenants within the same environment; cross-environment (staging-to-production) migration uses Configuration Exports per module with manual dependency sequencing ('Ensure that any dependencies... are imported or created beforehand').
notes: Also faq/configuration-migration. No version control, diffing, or approval gate on configuration changes.

claim: Third-party assessment: Open Loyalty 'demands developer resources to build the experience', deployment takes 'weeks to months', 'active-member pricing is opaque until you talk to sales', and the platform is enterprise-only ('overkill for standard ecommerce loyalty'); alternatives listed include Talon.One, Antavo, Capillary, Annex Cloud, Salesforce Loyalty, Smile.io, Yotpo.
notes: Single third-party source; consistent with official pricing page (sales-led) and API-first positioning.

claim: Adjacent competitor: Antavo - enterprise loyalty platform with 'API-first foundation' plus no-code workflows, AI loyalty planning, clients incl. KFC, Puma, SKIMS, C&A, Hyatt, Scandic (3M members, 7-tier migration); cited in Gartner Market Guide and Forrester Loyalty Landscape.
notes: Closest enterprise-loyalty competitor with stronger no-code positioning.

claim: Adjacent competitor: White Label Loyalty - 'AI-powered loyalty infrastructure' with event-based architecture ('100 million+ loyalty events'), API-first rules-driven engine delivering incentives 'in real time'; clients incl. PepsiCo, AkzoNobel, Burger King EMEA.
page_title: White Label Loyalty - Enterprise Loyalty Platform
notes: Event-driven loyalty engine directly comparable to Open Loyalty's architecture.

claim: API best-practices guidance covers retries with exponential backoff, 429 handling, ETag/Last-Modified caching, scroll pagination for large datasets, mandatory User-Agent header (requests without it are blocked at infrastructure level), and advises making POST/PATCH endpoints idempotent so 'clients can safely retry requests without causing unintended side effects' - but no Idempotency-Key header or documented server-side duplicate rejection (e.g., on documentNumber) was found.
page_title: Best Practices | Open Loyalty Technical Guide
notes: Idempotency guarantees remain unresolved (H06 = ?).

claim: Documented integration surface: Braze technology-partner integration (bidirectional: points, tier, segment updates), webhook delivery to AWS SQS, and worked integration examples for AWS Lambda, Zapier, AWS EventBridge, and Kafka.
page_title: Open Loyalty Technical Guide - sitemap (integration pages)
notes: Page existence verified via official sitemap; Braze partnership also confirmed by marketplace.braze.com listing. All integrations are marketing/data-pipeline oriented; none are identity/geo/fraud signal vendors.

claim: Absence inference: the complete official documentation index (238 user-guide pages, 67 technical-guide pages, 302 API-reference pages enumerated via sitemaps, plus llms.txt full index) contains no identity verification, age/address verification, geolocation, device intelligence, VPN detection, fraud scoring, case management, approval/maker-checker workflow, official-rules/AMOE/winner-drawing/tax-reporting, regulatory monitoring, legal-content, or infrastructure-as-code features.
notes: INFERENCE, labeled as such: treated as positive evidence of absence because the sitemaps enumerate the entire documented feature surface of the product. Used to justify 0 scores per brief rules.

claim: Rewards/redemption machinery: reward types with unit costs and coupons, reward flow with redeemed-reward status lifecycle and status-change history endpoint, bulk/mass status changes, cancel-redeemed-reward, get-eligible-members-list, per-reward visibility and limits, fortune-wheel draw endpoint.
page_title: Open Loyalty API Reference - sitemap (reward endpoints)
notes: Endpoint names verified via official API-reference sitemap; user-guide has reward-fulfillment section incl. mass reward status change.

claim: Custom events are first-class: admins define custom event schemas (with attribute identifiers usable in expressions as event.body.*), external systems POST custom events via API, and campaigns/achievements/webhooks react to them; endpoints include add-a-custom-event-schema, add-a-custom-event, get-custom-events-list.
page_title: Custom Event | Open Loyalty API Reference
notes: This is the generic event-ingestion mechanism that makes the engine adaptable to arbitrary domains (any action can be modeled as a custom event).

claim: Fully public REST API reference (apidocs.openloyalty.io / help.openloyalty.io/api-reference) documenting 300+ endpoints across ~30 tags (authorization, members, points, wallets, campaigns incl. simulate-campaigns-result, custom events, segments, tiers, rewards, audit, ACL, admin, analytics, webhooks, imports/exports, tenants/stores, bulk actions, health check); Postman collections maintained; REST is framework/language-agnostic.
notes: No official language SDKs found - integration is raw REST + Postman + MCP server.

claim: Docs ship a reusable configuration cookbook rather than product packs: 20+ sample campaign setups (earn rates, stamps, cashback, referral chains, tier-unlock), 7 sample achievement configurations, pay-with-points and promo-in-cart patterns, plus gamification modules (challenges, leaderboards with rewarding cycles, badges, tiers with benefits/analytics).
page_title: Open Loyalty User Guide - sitemap (sample setups, gamification)
notes: Templates are documentation recipes; no importable/marketplace policy-pack product.
